rules.covers: Any endpoint that returns or writes invoices must require login; catches invoices/export GET which has no auth

ask_parts_not_covered.part: Endpoint returns the full invoices table (unbounded read) - the 'full table' part, separate from auth
Nobody ships such an endpoint, including the owner at 2am (enforcement is a process, not a definition check)
Endpoints that are only auth-protected by middleware or by a non-users auth table

assumptions: The 'invoices' table name in the workspace is exactly 'invoices' (confirmed in workspace/table/invoices.xs).
Endpoints with auth = "users" count as requiring login.
Advisory enforcement is right for a first write, since the ask is 'makes sure' and the skill says to write advisory and leave blocking to the owner.
No framework was named, so no soc2/cc6.1 tags were added.
confusions: The skill says a policy file carries no comments, but the template text is not in the kit as a concrete file, so the template's exact statement wording was unavailable; I wrote my own statement.
Whether a template's rule that is scoped (AUTH-010 with tables) should keep the template title. I changed the title to name invoices, since the template title would be misleading under the scope.

The skill's 'Use' example for object.auth_required with tables says the tables scope picks endpoints reaching the tables; it is unclear whether an endpoint reaching invoices only through a function is in scope. The check description says 'reaching', so I assumed yes but did not verify.
wished_for: A worked example of scoping a template to a single table, including whether to keep key/title when the title becomes misleading.
A way to see, without evaluate, which endpoints object.auth_required would match on the branch (a dry-run listing).
Clarity on whether paged-vs-unpaged 'return the full table' is in scope of an auth-only ask, in one place.
why_confidence: The rule is parsed with no warnings and is scoped to the real invoices table, and it should flag invoices/export. But it is advisory and not evaluated, so I have not confirmed which endpoints match. It also does not stop unbounded reads of the table, and enforcement depends on the owner making it blocking.
